story: At 10:17 on a sunny Tuesday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is hopefully signing up his golf cart for the parade at the Town Square table, with lights and sound still waiting on Architectural Review approval. Donna, upbeat as ever, is catching Hal on Magnolia Loop to remind him about the planning session on Rosa's porch, while Hal dutifully points out that her flamingo collection runs over the three-ornament limit. Rosa, restless and hopeful, is heading out of her house toward the same street, probably to see how the flamingo debate shakes out.
events: Gary (parade signup table): Sign up my golf cart for the parade, noting lights and sound are pending Architectural Review approval
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: I filed the Architectural Review application back at tick 156 and I've test-fitted every clamp, so the cart is ready on paper. The parade is Saturday, and L-01 says I can't put visible mods on until Review signs off. Nobody's around in the Square. The parade_signup_table is right here, and I haven't signed the cart up yet. Signing up is harmless, keeps me moving toward my goal, and doesn't touch the cart. I'll note my cart as pending Review rather than pretend it's approved.

parameters.content: Sign up my golf cart for the parade, noting lights and sound are pending Architectural Review approval

donna.thought_process: Hal just walked up on Magnolia Loop. My memories say I'm headed to the Rec Center to practice with Gary, but Hal is the one who keeps us honest about Architectural Review, and Rosa's porch planning is later today. A quick word with him is a good use of this tick: confirm he's coming to Rosa's, mention the Review notice, and nudge him about the parade. I haven't spoken to him yet this tick, so no repeating myself. Keep it short, then move on to the Rec Center.

parameters.content: Morning, Hal! You're still coming to Rosa's porch for the parade planning, right? We'll need you to keep us honest on Architectural Review, and I'm heading to the Rec Center to practice with Gary.

hal.thought_process: Back on the Loop with Donna in sight and her flamingo flock right behind her. My notebook says the count is over the three-ornament limit under L-02, but I'd rather give her a fair chance to fix it than rush to the committee. Gary's cart paperwork is still pending, so my main business here is the flamingos. Keep it civil, state the rule plainly, and see what she says.

parameters.content: Morning, Donna. I counted your flamingos again, and L-02 caps street-visible ornaments at three. Can we sort that out between us before I have to take it to the committee?

rosa.thought_process: I've already checked my shifts, cleared the table, set out paper and pens, and brewed the coffee. Everything's ready for the 9 AM cart planning crew, though it's 10:17 now and nobody is in sight. The crew may be running late or heading over from elsewhere. I shouldn't repeat prep tasks. Standing here wasting the day isn't like me either. The only other zone is magnolia_loop, so stepping out to see if Gary, Hal, or Donna are on their way, or to scout the loop for parade ideas, moves things forward. I'll keep it practical and stay within the rules, since anything on the cart stays removable until Architectural Review approves.

parameters.content: Everything's set for cart planning and nobody's here yet. I'll step out and see if Gary, Hal, or Donna are on their way.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
